chapter: Learning trombone and the Wisconsin Roof years
title: First trombone and lessons from William Robinson, Dutre and Roy
summary: His first teacher gave him a trombone; he then learned from Dutre and Roy Palmer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Oh well, it's between, well my first teacher, I'd forgotten him, was William Robinson. What's his name?

He was from God? Yeah, you see, I didn't care for the trombone when I did become interested, because I used to whistle a lot of clarinet parts, I'd say. And right up until there I can do that. And so Joe told me, I said, well, you used to get stuff from me. Joe said, partner says, you don't need no trombone for that. See, that's clarinet. And so I talked to my mother concerning the clarinet, but this William Robinson, he was a trombonist, and his wife and my mother were great friends. So I returned home one evening, I'd say in the afternoon, and I walked inside and I walked into my room and I saw a little green bag. And so I went there, kind of curious, you know. I knew it was too loud for clarinet, so I opened the band, there was a little Carl Fisher, a trombone, see. So this Robinson, my first lessons were held. But I left him and went to Dutre and Roy.
Dutre taught you how to read?
